comment: Apps added to the library by hand, outside the 3-Lib CD-ROM.
catalogue.json holds the CD's own index verbatim, so anything that
wasn't on the CD is catalogued here instead.
scripts/build-app-library.mts merges these entries into the
catalogue of the category named below; `dir` is the app's folder
inside applib/<category>/ and everything else mirrors a catalogue
entry (date in the CD's DD/MM/YY dialect).
`devices` and `tryDevice` are optional per-app overrides of the
category defaults, for apps that don't run on the whole family.
`sisPayloads` names SIS installers elsewhere in the library whose
payloads are unpacked into the bundle at the paths the SIS itself
declares — for shared libraries an installed-folder app needs at
The `netpad` category is absent from catalogue.json (it was never
on the CD): every one of its entries lives here.

apps.name: Wall (installed)
apps.description: The Breakout clone catalogued above as WALL, in ready-to-run form: the \System\Apps\Wall folder off a device (a later, 2007 build) instead of a SIS installer, so it is copied into place rather than installed. Includes the owner's USER.REG registration file, which unlocks all 18 levels and the hard difficulty on the machine whose Unique id the code was issued for.

apps.name: Monopoly
apps.description: The property-trading board game for the Series 5 family, in ready-to-run form: the \System\Apps\Monopoly folder as it sits on a device rather than a SIS installer, so it is copied into place instead of installed. Five boards (English, American, French, German and Dutch street names), seven computer opponents with their own playing styles, digitised sound and an on-device help file.

apps.name: Agenda
apps.description: The EPOC diary: day, week, month and year views, timed and untimed entries, repeats, alarms, anniversaries and to-do lists. Ships with the netpad Agenda manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Calc
apps.description: The EPOC calculator, in both its desk and scientific modes, with memories and a tape of previous results. Ships with the netpad Calc manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Comms
apps.description: The terminal emulator: VT100 sessions over the serial port or a modem, scripted logins, and file transfer by XMODEM, YMODEM or ZMODEM. Ships with the netpad Comms manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Contacts
apps.description: The EPOC address book, with per-contact labels, search-as-you-type and its own printing and vCard exchange. Ships with the netpad Contacts manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Data (manual)
apps.description: The netpad Data manual — the free-form database's documentation, as a PDF. Documentation only, and deliberately so: Data is the one application the netpad's ROM does carry (it is in Extras on a fresh machine), so the CD ships its manual without an installer.

apps.name: Email
apps.description: The EPOC Message Suite mail client (\System\Apps\MsgApp): POP3, IMAP4 and SMTP accounts, plus fax and SMS message types, with folders held in a local message store. Ships with the netpad Email manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Jotter
apps.description: The quick-notes application: one list of jottings per file, each expandable into a full note. Ships with the netpad Jotter manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Record
apps.description: The sound recorder: record, play back and trim WVE clips, and set one as an alarm sound. Ships with the netpad Record manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Sheet
apps.description: The EPOC spreadsheet: formulae and functions, named blocks, charts and its own printing, reading and writing the Psion .SPD format. Ships with the netpad Sheet manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Sketch
apps.description: The drawing application (installed by paint.sis): freehand pen, shapes, fills and text on a resizable canvas, saved as an EPOC sketch. Ships with the netpad Sketch manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Spell
apps.description: The spelling checker, thesaurus and anagram/crossword solver, usable on its own or from inside Word. Ships with the netpad Spell manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Time
apps.description: Alarms, the world clock and its city database of times, dialling codes and distances. Ships with the netpad Time manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Word
apps.description: The EPOC word processor: styles, outlining, tables of contents, embedded objects and its own printing, reading and writing the Psion .WRD format. Ships with the netpad Word manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Program editor
apps.description: The OPL program editor (texted.sis) — write, translate and run OPL programs on the device itself. Ships with the netpad Programming manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Program editor (March 2002)
apps.description: An earlier build of the OPL program editor above, with the same Programming manual. Kept as the CD shipped it — install the December 2002 build unless you specifically want this one.

apps.name: Opera
apps.description: The Opera web browser for EPOC — the netpad's graphical browser, installed alongside its plug-in and font support. Ships with the netpad Opera manual as a PDF.

apps.name: Java
apps.description: Symbian's PersonalJava runtime for EPOC: the JVM itself (JavaRun, appletviewer, rmiregistry), the class libraries, and the recognisers and browser plug-in that let EPOC start a .jar or an applet from a link.

apps.name: nFTP
apps.description: An FTP client for EPOC — browse a remote server and transfer files over the netpad's own network connection.

apps.name: Barcode
apps.description: Psion Teklogix barcode-scanner support for the netpad, plus the scandemo application that shows the decoded scans. The demo runs without a scanner attached; reading real barcodes needs the hardware.

apps.name: Signapp
apps.description: Signature capture for the netpad's pen: sign on the screen and keep the signature with the record it belongs to — one of the vertical-market applications the tablet was sold for.
